**3. MEMBERSHIP**

3.1 Membership of the Club shall be open to all persons aged 16 years and over who are approved by the Committee in accordance with this Constitution. No person shall be excluded from membership on discriminatory grounds.

3.2 The following categories of membership shall exist:

(a) **Full Member** – open to persons aged 18 years and over. Full Members may vote at General Meetings, stand for election to the Committee, and use all Club facilities.

(b) **Junior Member** – open to persons aged 16 and 17 years. Junior Members may use Club facilities but may not vote at General Meetings or stand for election to the Committee.

(c) **Social Member** – open to persons aged 18 years and over who wish to use the Clubhouse and social facilities only, and who do not participate in organised sporting activities. Social Members may not vote at General Meetings.

(d) **Life Member** – conferred by the Committee, at its absolute discretion, upon a person who has rendered outstanding service to the Club. Life Members enjoy all the privileges of Full Members.

(e) **Honorary Member** – conferred by the Committee, at its absolute discretion, upon a person for a period not exceeding one year. Honorary Members enjoy such privileges as the Committee may determine in each case.

3.3 Applications for membership shall be made in writing, on the form provided by the Club Secretary, and shall be accompanied by the appropriate subscription. The Committee shall consider each application at its next meeting and shall notify the applicant of its decision in writing within 14 days of that meeting.

3.4 The Committee shall have the power to refuse any application for membership without stating a reason, provided that such refusal shall not be on discriminatory grounds. Any applicant refused membership may appeal in writing to the Chair of the Committee within 21 days of receiving the refusal notice. The appeal shall be heard at the next Committee meeting, at which the applicant may make representations in person.

**15. FINANCE**

15.1 The financial year of the Club shall end on 31st March in each year.

15.2 The Treasurer shall cause proper books of account to be kept with respect to:

(a) all sums of money received and expended by the Club and the matters in respect of which such receipt and expenditure takes place;

(b) all sales and purchases of goods by the Club;

(c) the assets and liabilities of the Club.

15.3 The books of account shall be kept at such place as the Committee may determine and shall be open to inspection by any Committee member at all reasonable times.

15.4 The Treasurer shall present an interim financial report to the Committee at each ordinary Committee meeting.

The independent examiner shall report to the members at the next Annual General Meeting on the accounts examined and on the statement and balance sheet presented under clause 15.5.

15.7 The income and property of the Club, whencesoever derived, shall be applied solely towards the promotion of the objects of the Club as set out in clause 2. 15.8 The Committee shall have power to authorise the payment of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred by officers, Committee members, or other members in connection with the business of the Club, including but not limited to travel expenses, postage, and telephone calls.

15.9 No officer or Committee member shall be personally liable for the debts or liabilities of the Club except to the extent that such debts or liabilities have been incurred as a result of that person’s own negligence, fraud, or breach of duty.

15.10 The Committee shall cause to be maintained a petty cash float, the amount of which shall be fixed by the Committee from time to time. All payments from the petty cash float shall be recorded in a petty cash book and supported by receipts wherever practicable.

15.11 All cheques, drafts, and other orders for the payment of money shall be signed by not fewer than two authorised signatories, one of whom shall be the Treasurer or, in the Treasurer’s absence, the Chair. The Committee shall keep a current list of authorised signatories and shall review such list at least once per financial year.

15.12 The Club shall maintain a bank account, or accounts, in the name of the Club. No bank account shall be opened or closed except by resolution of the Committee. The Committee shall be notified of the terms of all such accounts and of any change therein.

15.13 The Committee may, by resolution, establish a separate account or accounts for specific purposes, including but not limited to junior sections, social events, or capital projects. Any such account shall be under the control of the Committee and shall be subject to the same provisions as to signatories and accounting as the principal account.
16. DISSOLUTION

16.1 The Club may be dissolved by resolution passed at a General Meeting of the Club, provided that:

(a) notice of the motion for dissolution has been given in writing to the Secretary at least twenty-eight days before the meeting at which the motion is to be considered;

(b) the resolution is passed by not less than two-thirds of those present and voting at the meeting; and

(c) the meeting at which the resolution is passed is quorate in accordance with Clause 8.

16.2 Upon a resolution for dissolution being passed, the Committee shall take immediate steps to wind up the affairs of the Club, including the collection of all outstanding debts and the discharge of all liabilities.

16.3 After the discharge of all liabilities, any surplus assets remaining shall not be distributed among the members but shall be transferred to such charitable or community sports body or bodies, or applied to such purposes connected with sport or recreation, as the dissolution meeting shall by the same or a subsequent resolution determine. In default of any such determination, the surplus assets shall be transferred to the governing body of the sport or sports with which the Club is principally concerned, to be held and applied for the promotion of that sport.

16.4 A copy of the resolution for dissolution and of any resolution under Clause 16.3 shall be lodged with the appropriate authorities as required by law.

16.5 The Committee shall retain the books, records, and accounts of the Club for a period of not less than six years following dissolution, after which they may be destroyed.

17. LIABILITY AND INDEMNITY

17.1 The liability of members is limited to the amount of their subscriptions and any other sums properly due to the Club. No member shall be liable to contribute towards the assets of the Club upon dissolution beyond any amounts then unpaid on their account.

17.2 The Club shall indemnify every officer and Committee member against all costs, charges, losses, expenses, and liabilities incurred by them in the execution of their duties, save where such costs, charges, losses, expenses, or liabilities arise from their own negligence, fraud, or breach of duty.

17.3 The Committee may, at the expense of the Club, maintain insurance policies for the benefit of officers, Committee members, and volunteers, including but not limited to public liability insurance, employer’s liability insurance, and personal accident cover for members engaged in Club activities.

17.4 Nothing in this Constitution shall be construed as creating a partnership between the members, officers, or Committee members of the Club.

18. MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS

18.1 The headings in this Constitution are for convenience only and shall not affect its interpretation.

18.2 Words importing the singular shall include the plural and vice versa, and words importing any gender shall include all genders, unless the context otherwise requires.

18.3 References to any statute or statutory provision shall be construed as references to that statute or provision as amended, re-enacted, or replaced from time to time.

18.4 Any notice required to be given to a member under this Constitution shall be deemed duly given if sent by post, email, or other electronic means to the address last notified by the member to the Secretary.

18.5 A member may appoint a proxy to attend and vote on their behalf at any General Meeting, provided that the instrument appointing the proxy is deposited with the Secretary not less than forty-eight hours before the meeting.

18.6 The Committee may from time to time make, alter, and rescind bye-laws for the regulation of the Club, provided that no bye-law shall be inconsistent with the provisions of this Constitution. All bye-laws shall be reported to the next General Meeting and shall remain in force unless and until revoked by that meeting.

**3. MEMBERSHIP**

3.1 Membership of the Club shall be open to all persons aged 16 years and over who are approved by the Committee in accordance with this Constitution. No person shall be excluded from membership on discriminatory grounds.

3.2 The following categories of membership shall exist:

(a) **Full Member** – open to persons aged 18 years and over. Full Members may vote at General Meetings, stand for election to the Committee, and use all Club facilities.

(b) **Junior Member** – open to persons aged 16 and 17 years. Junior Members may use Club facilities but may not vote at General Meetings or stand for election to the Committee.

(c) **Social Member** – open to persons aged 18 years and over who wish to use the Clubhouse and social facilities only, and who do not participate in organised sporting activities. Social Members may not vote at General Meetings.

(d) **Life Member** – conferred by the Committee, at its absolute discretion, upon a person who has rendered outstanding service to the Club. Life Members enjoy all the privileges of Full Members.

(e) **Honorary Member** – conferred by the Committee, at its absolute discretion, upon a person for a period not exceeding one year. Honorary Members enjoy such privileges as the Committee may determine in each case.

3.3 Applications for membership shall be made in writing, on the form provided by the Club Secretary, and shall be accompanied by the appropriate subscription. The Committee shall consider each application at its next meeting and shall notify the applicant of its decision in writing within 14 days of that meeting.

3.4 The Committee shall have the power to refuse any application for membership without stating a reason, provided that such refusal shall not be on discriminatory grounds. Any applicant refused membership may appeal in writing to the Chair of the Committee within 21 days of receiving the refusal notice. The appeal shall be heard at the next Committee meeting, at which the applicant may make representations in person.

3.5 The annual subscription for each category of membership shall be fixed by the Committee from time to time, subject to ratification by the members at the Annual General Meeting. Any change to subscription rates shall take effect from the first day of the membership year.

3.6 The membership year shall run from 1 April to 31 March.

3.7 A member may resign by giving written notice to the Club Secretary. No refund of subscription shall be payable.

3.8 The Committee may terminate the membership of any person whose conduct, in the opinion of the Committee, is detrimental to the interests of the Club. The member concerned shall be given 14 days’ written notice of the Committee’s intention to consider termination, and shall be entitled to make representations in person at the meeting at which the matter is considered. The member shall have a further right of appeal to a Special General Meeting called for that purpose, such appeal to be lodged in writing within 21 days of the Committee’s decision.

15.4 The Treasurer shall present an interim financial report to the Committee at each ordinary Committee meeting.

15.5 At the Annual General Meeting, the Treasurer shall present a statement of income and expenditure for the previous financial year and a balance sheet as at the end of that financial year. Such statement and balance sheet shall have been examined by the independent examiner appointed under clause 15.6.

15.6 An independent examiner, who shall not be a member of the Committee, shall be appointed at each Annual General Meeting to examine the accounts of the Club for the ensuing financial year. The independent examiner shall be a person who is, in the opinion of the Committee, suitably qualified for the purpose. The independent examiner shall report to the members at the next Annual General Meeting on the accounts examined and on the statement and balance sheet presented under clause 15.5.

15.7 The income and property of the Club, whencesoever derived, shall be applied solely towards the promotion of the objects of the Club as set out in clause 2. No portion thereof shall be paid or transferred, directly or indirectly, by way of dividend, bonus, or otherwise howsoever by way of profit to members of the Club, provided that nothing herein shall prevent the payment in good faith of reasonable and proper remuneration to any officer or servant of the Club, or of interest on money lent, or of reasonable and proper rent for premises demised or let to the Club.

15.8 The Committee shall have power to authorise the payment of reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred by officers, Committee members, or other members in connection with the business of the Club, including but not limited to travel expenses, postage, and telephone calls.

15.9 No officer or Committee member shall be personally liable for the debts or liabilities of the Club except to the extent that such debts or liabilities have been incurred as a result of that person’s own negligence, fraud, or breach of duty.

15.10 The Committee shall cause to be maintained a petty cash float, the amount of which shall be fixed by the Committee from time to time. All payments from the petty cash float shall be recorded in a petty cash book and supported by receipts wherever practicable.

15.11 All cheques, drafts, and other orders for the payment of money shall be signed by not fewer than two authorised signatories, one of whom shall be the Treasurer or, in the Treasurer’s absence, the Chair. The Committee shall keep a current list of authorised signatories and shall review such list at least once per financial year.

15.12 The Club shall maintain a bank account, or accounts, in the name of the Club. No bank account shall be opened or closed except by resolution of the Committee. The Committee shall be notified of the terms of all such accounts and of any change therein.

15.13 The Committee may, by resolution, establish a separate account or accounts for specific purposes, including but not limited to junior sections, social events, or capital projects. Any such account shall be under the control of the Committee and shall be subject to the same provisions as to signatories and accounting as the principal account.

16. DISSOLUTION

16.1 The Club may be dissolved by resolution passed at a General Meeting of the Club, provided that:

(a) notice of the motion for dissolution has been given in writing to the Secretary at least twenty-eight days before the meeting at which the motion is to be considered;

(b) the resolution is passed by not less than two-thirds of those present and voting at the meeting; and

(c) the meeting at which the resolution is passed is quorate in accordance with Clause 8.

16.2 Upon a resolution for dissolution being passed, the Committee shall take immediate steps to wind up the affairs of the Club, including the collection of all outstanding debts and the discharge of all liabilities.

16.3 After the discharge of all liabilities, any surplus assets remaining shall not be distributed among the members but shall be transferred to such charitable or community sports body or bodies, or applied to such purposes connected with sport or recreation, as the dissolution meeting shall by the same or a subsequent resolution determine. In default of any such determination, the surplus assets shall be transferred to the governing body of the sport or sports with which the Club is principally concerned, to be held and applied for the promotion of that sport.

16.4 A copy of the resolution for dissolution and of any resolution under Clause 16.3 shall be lodged with the appropriate authorities as required by law.

16.5 The Committee shall retain the books, records, and accounts of the Club for a period of not less than six years following dissolution, after which they may be destroyed.

17. LIABILITY AND INDEMNITY

17.1 The liability of members is limited to the amount of their subscriptions and any other sums properly due to the Club. No member shall be liable to contribute towards the assets of the Club upon dissolution beyond any amounts then unpaid on their account.

17.2 The Club shall indemnify every officer and Committee member against all costs, charges, losses, expenses, and liabilities incurred by them in the execution of their duties, save where such costs, charges, losses, expenses, or liabilities arise from their own negligence, fraud, or breach of duty.

17.3 The Committee may, at the expense of the Club, maintain insurance policies for the benefit of officers, Committee members, and volunteers, including but not limited to public liability insurance, employer’s liability insurance, and personal accident cover for members engaged in Club activities.

17.4 Nothing in this Constitution shall be construed as creating a partnership between the members, officers, or Committee members of the Club.

18. MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS

18.1 The headings in this Constitution are for convenience only and shall not affect its interpretation.

18.2 Words importing the singular shall include the plural and vice versa, and words importing any gender shall include all genders, unless the context otherwise requires.

18.3 References to any statute or statutory provision shall be construed as references to that statute or provision as amended, re-enacted, or replaced from time to time.

18.4 Any notice required to be given to a member under this Constitution shall be deemed duly given if sent by post, email, or other electronic means to the address last notified by the member to the Secretary.

18.5 A member may appoint a proxy to attend and vote on their behalf at any General Meeting, provided that the instrument appointing the proxy is deposited with the Secretary not less than forty-eight hours before the meeting.

18.6 The Committee may from time to time make, alter, and rescind bye-laws for the regulation of the Club, provided that no bye-law shall be inconsistent with the provisions of this Constitution. All bye-laws shall be reported to the next General Meeting and shall remain in force unless and until revoked by that meeting.
